finding: The round-5 rewrite of §8.2 removed the baseline branch that named `--resolve-all`/`--resolve <idx>` as the next_action for convergence-blocking findings; the new blocking branch is a revise-the-spec directive that 'never steers toward `--resolve`/`--resolve-all`', and new Test 14 explicitly asserts next_action 'never names `--resolve`/`--resolve-all`/`--verify`'. So no next_action branch ever names `--resolve-all`. But three UNCHANGED framing sections still present next_action as the mechanism that un-buries `--resolve-all`: Principle 6 ('rather than burying `--verify`, `--resolve-all`, and check registration'), §8.1's problem statement ('so `--verify`, `--resolve-all`, and check registration get read past' → 'gain a next_action'), and the Overview table row for `--resolve-all`/`--verify` ('never as the next action | §8: next_action'). In the round-4 baseline these were consistent because §8.2 item 2 did name `--resolve-all`; the round-5 change undid that surfacing without reconciling the unchanged framing, which now over-promises what next_action does.
suggestion: Reconcile the unchanged framing with the new §8.2. Either narrow Principle 6 / §8.1 / the Overview row to say next_action surfaces check registration (and the next-step commands) while `--resolve-all`/`--verify` are surfaced via the §8.3/§9 documentation adjacent to `--resolve` (not via next_action, by design so blocking findings are never auto-advised toward disposal), or add an explicit note in §8.2 that next_action deliberately does not name `--resolve-all` and that its discoverability lives in the docs.

finding: §3.4 says `--record` persists a per-round clean flag that is the fallback for a round carrying no per-finding severity, and Test 5 asserts that for 'a new round where every finding omitted severity' the 'persisted clean flag is honored'. But the spec never states the RULE by which `--record` COMPUTES that flag at record time for such a round. §4.1's conservative 'missing severity = blocking' per-finding rule explicitly does NOT apply here (it is superseded by the round-level fallback when no finding carries a severity). So two engineers writing Test 5's new-round arm cannot agree on the expected value: one computes clean=true (no blocking severity is present, so nothing blocks under `blocking`), letting a round full of findings count toward convergence; another computes clean=false (findings exist under `all`-like/legacy semantics). The expected before/after is unpinned, so the test is not deterministically writable.
suggestion: State explicitly how `--record` computes the persisted clean flag for a new round in which every finding omits severity — e.g. 'a severity-less new round is recorded clean=false (treated as `all`) so a fully severity-less panel can never silently converge', or name the exact policy used — so Test 5's new-round arm has a determinate expected value.

finding: Precedence branch 3 (a `mechanize_candidates` class present, none blocking -> `register a check`) outranks branch 4 (`run the next round`), but the action it names — `tp set --workflow checks='[…]'` — records no new round and does not alter the recorded findings that produce the `mechanize_candidates` array (defined as a class that recurs across recorded rounds). So on the next `--status`/`--record` the state is unchanged and `next_action` returns branch 3 again. The precedence is total but non-progressing: an agent that follows `next_action` (its whole purpose, §8.1 / Principle 6) is pinned at 'register a check' and never reaches branch 4 to record another round or accumulate clean rounds toward convergence. The spec never states that registering a check clears the `mechanize_candidates` signal, nor that branch 3 should combine register-then-run — so an implementer building the precedence function must invent the exit condition. Distinct from the backlog entries about the *definition/trigger* of `mechanize_candidates`; this is about the branch having no progress rule.
suggestion: Pin down how branch 3 is left. Either (a) make branch 3 a compound directive that registers the check AND runs the next round (`register a check, then run the next review round: … tp review <spec> --record <file>`), so following it records a round and re-derives the signal; or (b) state that a `mechanize_candidates` class for which a matching check is already registered no longer counts toward the branch-3 signal, so once the agent registers the check the branch falls through to branch 4. State the chosen rule explicitly in §8.2 and cover the transition in Test 14.

finding: §4.2 introduces `nonblocking_open` with a conditional trigger — 'When a round is clean only because its surviving findings are all below the blocking severities, --status and --record ... carry nonblocking_open'. §8.4, by contrast, treats `nonblocking_open` as a standard always-present field that 'survives compaction' alongside `next_action`. The two sections disagree on whether the key is emitted only on the clean-with-nonblocking case or on every round (as 0 when none, present even on a non-clean round that still has surviving medium/low findings). A test author cannot deterministically assert the key's presence/absence for a non-clean round or a zero-finding clean round, and JSON-schema stability (is the key always present?) is left open.
suggestion: Pin the emission condition: state whether `nonblocking_open` is emitted on every --status/--record response (0 when no surviving non-blocking findings) or only when the round is clean-with-surviving-nonblocking, and reconcile §4.2's conditional wording with §8.4's always-retained framing so the JSON contract is testable across all round states.

finding: `nonblocking_open` is emitted unconditionally on every --status/--record and explicitly survives --compact, but both §4.2 and §8.4 tie its decision-value strictly to a clean round: §4.2 ("a clean round with nonblocking_open > 0 is one where non-blocking findings were accepted open") and §8.4 ("the count an operator weighs to proceed-or-resolve, tied to the current convergence decision"). On a blocking (non-clean) round the agent's next step is 'revise the spec' (§8.2 branch 2) — a decision nonblocking_open does not feed — yet the count is still emitted and still survives compaction there. That is an always-on, compact-surviving byte whose own stated justification applies only at clean/converged rounds, which fails the AX lens for the default-compact agent on every non-clean round.
suggestion: State that nonblocking_open is decision-bearing only when the round is clean, and either emit it (or at least retain it under --compact) only on clean rounds, or add a sentence to §8.4 explicitly scoping its compact-survival to clean rounds so the field can be dropped from compact output on blocking rounds.
